title: Metropolis
synopsis: A city of towers, a workers' city below, a robot of a woman in a chair, and a flood about to rise into the children's lobby.

nodes.text: A peacock fountain and a girl from below at the elevator. The road still runs toward Machine M. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Follow her” and choosing “Stay.” At Machine M, the decision will matter as data as well as intent.

choices.consequence: You commit to follow her. It carries you toward Machine M, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to stay. It carries you toward Machine M, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Sun on the towers, a city that has stopped flooding, a small calm. “Breathe” opens the route to Hand on Hand on Hand. “Get to work” changes the terms and carries you toward Lobby of the Saved. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Catacombs Empty in play.

choices.consequence: You breathe. The path to Hand on Hand on Hand opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to get to work. It carries you toward Lobby of the Saved, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You choose to take the third path. By Catacombs Empty, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The owner and the foreman take each other's hands with a son between them and the city, briefly, learns a new manner of being a city. The road into Hand on Hand on Hand began with “Breathe” in Dawn; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You stand in a soaked lobby with children at your knees and a woman across the room who is also you, somehow, and you all breathe. The road into Lobby of the Saved began with “Get to work” in Dawn; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You return to the candles and the crucifix alone and you sit there a long time, and you do not preach to anyone, and that is also a kind of answer. The road into Catacombs Empty began with “Take the third path” in Dawn; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.
